electricity connection on an overload of 787 Kw instead of sanctioned

demand had been raised in respect of 51 months there was no basis for 
calculating average overload for 51 months. Further it was held that if, the 
consumer was found to be consuming excess electricity than the 
sanctioned load, then it was incumbent upon the petitioner to include the 
amount payable against the overload in the monthly bills raised against 
the consumer at the tariff rate determined by the Electricity Regulatory 
Commission and on failure to raise such demand timely, it is the failure 
on the part of the officer of the concerned Distribution Division and an 
inquiry in this regard ought to have been conducted. The learned Forum 
while relying upon Section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 
6.15 of the U.P. Electricity Supply code, 2005 has held that the 
respondent no. 2 could not have been held liable to pay the alleged arrears 
on account of overload for the past 51 months. Under the circumstances 
the Forum had set aside the demand raised by means of letter dated 
07.09.2022 and had further directed the Chief Engineer (Distribution), 
Aligarh to take appropriate action in respect of matter relating to failure to 
raise timely demands of revenue in respect of the excess load.
5. The petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned order has filed this 
writ petition on the ground that the demand of Rs.1,83,516/- was in due 
accordance with the provisions of para 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply 
Code, 2005 and under the circumstances the impugned order dated 
14.08.2013 is not sustainable in the eyes of law.
6. Per contra it has been claimed on behalf of the respondent no.2 that the 
impugned order is in due consonance with law as the check meter was 
WRIC No. 61368 of 2013
2

===== PAGE 4 =====
installed only for the duration of 02.09.2012 to 12.09.2012 and on the 
basis of the same the determination had been made in respect of 51 
months. Even though under the rules the assessment could have only been 
made for the period of one year. In this regard the respondent no.2 has 
relied upon the letter dated 02.03.2013 issued by the Chief Engineer 
(Distribution), Aligarh. Besides it is also contended that in the electricity 
meter installed in the premises of respondent no.2 a demand of 9.8 kw 
(UC) was being shown whereas in the check meter installed a demand of 
6.1 kw had been shown thereby clearly establishing the check meter was 
defective and had failed to record the correct reading. In this regard the 
respondent no.2 has relied upon the letter dated 09.03.2013 issued by the 
Chief Engineer (Distribution).
7. We have perused the records of the case.
8. Section 5.6 of the Electricity Act, 2003 reads as under:
"56. Disconnection of Supply in default of payment:-
(1).....
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time 
being in force, no sum due from any consumer, under this section shall be 
recoverable after the period of two years from the date when such sum 
became first due unless such sum has been shown continuously as 
recoverable as arrears of charges for electricity supplied and the licensee 
shall not cut off the supply of the electricity. "
9. Further the explanation to Clause 6.15 (b) of the U.P. Electricity 
Supply Code, 2005 reads as under:-
"6.15 Recovery of Arrears:-
(a)....
(b)....
[(Explanation: The date from which such charges becomes 'first due', 
needs to be correctly interpreted. If as a result meter reading/ inspection 
of installation of consumer, such charges/ penalties levied as per this 
code or tariff schedule, such became first due counted from the due date 
of payment of such a bill, and such bill shall be provided to the consumer 
WRIC No. 61368 of 2013
3

===== PAGE 5 =====
not later than two billing cycle for that category of consumer)]" 
10. We have also considered the letter dated 02.03.2013 issued on behalf 
of the Chief Engineer (Distribution) relevant part whereof reads as under:-
"प्रबन्ध निदेशक महोदय, द०वि०वि०नि०लि०, आगरा ने निर्देशित किया है कि विद्युत प्रदाय 
संहिता 2005 में दिये गये प्राविधानों के अनुसार अधिकतम एक वर्ष राजस्व निर्धारण किया जा 
सकता है। अतः मुझे आपसे यह कहने के निर्देश प्राप्त हुए हैं कि संलग्न पत्र में दिये गये निर्देशों 
के अनुरूप तत्काल राजस्व निर्धारण संशोधित कर इस कार्यालय के सूचनाधीन उपभोक्ता को 
अवगत करा दें।"
11. Thus, it is beyond doubt that it was not open for the petitioner to have 
raised the demand of overload in respect of 51 months. We cannot also 
lose sight of the fact that the Chief Engineer (Distribution) in his letter 
dated 09.03.2013 itself admitted that the check meter installed at the 
premises of the respondent no.2 was defective and was not recording the 
correct reading.
12. Thus, we are of the view that there was no infirmity in the impugned 
order dated 14.08.2013 passed by the learned Forum.
13. The writ petition lacks merits and is accordingly dismissed.
